PM SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 Recognise Excellence in Strengthening Street Vendors’ Livelihoods
articles.full_content:
The Department of Urban Development, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA), Government of India, will organise the SVANidhi Samman Awards 2026 on 20 November 2026 at the Dr. Ambedkar International Centre, New Delhi. The awards will be conferred by Shri Manohar Lal, Hon’ble Minister of Housing and Urban Affairs, in the presence of Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, as Guest of Honour.
Featuring 52 awards and 5 special recognitions , the event will honour the outstanding contributions of States/UTs, Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Lending Institutions and partner organisations in strengthening street vendors’ livelihoods and advancing financial inclusion, digital adoption and social security. Around 600 participants , representing various stakeholders associated with the Scheme, are expected to attend. The awards will recognise excellence across the following categories:
• States/UTs: 27 Awards to 16 States and 3 UTs
• Urban Local Bodies: 21 Awards
• Lending Institutions: 4 Awards
• Key Stakeholders: 5 Special Recognitions
Since its launch on 1 June 2020, PM SVANidhi has enabled around 81 lakh street vendors to access over 1.21 crore loans amounting to approximately ₹20,000 crore . In August 2025, the Government restructured the Scheme and extended its implementation up to March 2030, introducing key reforms to expand its reach and deepen financial inclusion. These include:
• Enhanced loan amounts across all three loan tranches to meet the evolving credit requirements of street vendors.
• Introduction of a UPI-linked RuPay Credit Card with a credit limit of up to ₹30,000 for eligible beneficiaries who have repaid their second loan tranche.
• Expansion of geographical coverage beyond statutory towns to include Census Towns and peri-urban areas.
Beyond credit support, the Scheme promotes the holistic socio-economic development of street vendor families through SVANidhi se Samriddhi . Socio-economic profiling of over 52 lakh beneficiary families has been completed, resulting in more than 1.62 crore sanctions under eight Central Government welfare schemes. The Scheme is also strengthening the street vending ecosystem through initiatives such as the development of 50 Street Food Hubs and capacity-building programmes, including food safety and hygiene training.

Advancing Global Statistical Partnerships: MoSPI’s Vision for Knowledge Exchange and Institutional Cooperation

MoSPI’s transformative Initiatives on SDGs and Statistical Database Stewardship for fortifying the architecture of India’s National Statistical System showcased
Reaffirming India’s abiding commitment to partnership and shared progress in the field of official statistics, the National Statistical Systems Training Academy (NSSTA)- Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), in collaboration with the National Institute of Labour Economics Research and Development (NILERD), organised an interaction of international participants from twenty-six partner countries of the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation (ITEC) Programme on 17 November 2026. The engagement offered the visiting delegates a meaningful vantage point on the manner in which India builds, governs and sustains its statistical institutions.
The occasion was graced by the eminent presence of Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics) and Dr. Purnendu Kishore Banerjee, Director General (Data Governance)-In-Charge, MoSPI, along with senior officers of the Ministry, including Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division and Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, Social Statistics Division. Dr. P. C. Parida, Director, NILERD and faculty of NILERD also participated.
Setting the tone for the day’s deliberations, Shri R. Rajesh, Additional Director General, Capacity Development Division recalled India’s timeless message that the world is one family and that all people are one’s own kin. Anchored in this civilisational outlook, he stressed that the country has consistently striven to extend its support to other nations in improving and strengthening their statistical systems. Ms. Reena Singh, Deputy Director General, NSSTA, while moderating the interaction, emphasized the crucial role of MoSPI in strengthening the country’s official statistical system ensuring the availability of reliable, credible and timely statistical information, and supporting evidence based policymaking across sectors. She also emphasized the pivotal role of NSSTA for strengthening the capacity of the statistical system in India.
The keynote address, delivered by Dr. Dalip Singh, Director General (Central Statistics), furnished the delegates with a comprehensive panorama of the National Statistical System of India. In the course of his address, he elaborated on the institutional framework, the organisational structure and the functioning of the Statistical System, thereby giving an overview of the various statistical products and varied surveys undertaken by MoSPI.
The substantive core of the interaction consisted of two technical sessions. The first session on “Overview of SDG Monitoring in India” was led by Ms. Supriya Roy, Additional Director General, SSD, Ms. Ruchika Gupta, Deputy Director General, SSD, and Shri Indradeep Roy Chaudhary, Director, SSD. DGFT Chennai Organises State-Level Workshop on Leveraging Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) to Boost Exports from Puducherry
articles.full_content:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT), Chennai, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, jointly with the Government of Puducherry, conducted a State-Level Workshop titled “Leveraging FTAs – Outreach Program” at Puducherry on 19.11.2026. The programme was aimed at spreading awareness on global trade opportunities and helping Puducherry’s exporters become more competitive in international markets.
Around 200 participants took part in the workshop, including exporters, MSME representatives, Export Promotion Councils and Chambers of Commerce
Thiru N. Rangasamy, Chief Minister of Puducherry, presiding over the ceremony, stressed that most of the exports from Puducherry were made by MSMEs; which provided employment opportunities to a lot of people. Even though Puducherry has small area, it was able to achieve exports worth Rs. 5000 cr last year.
The Chief Minister also declared a plan to set up an SEZ in an area of 250 acres which would further increase exports and employment. He said the export facilities at Karaikal Port will make shipping simpler and smoother for Puducherry’s exporters. With the right support and awareness, he also mentioned that Puducherry’ exports would grow steadily in the years ahead.
Smt. Rajalakshmi Devraj, Additional Director General of Foreign Trade, Regional Authority, Chennai, highlighted the significant opportunities arising from India's nine newly concluded Free Trade Agreements, which provide access to international markets with a combined GDP of approximately US$60 trillion. She emphasised the importance of strengthening India's export performance in line with the US$1 trillion export target for the current year and the vision of achieving a US$30 trillion economy by 2047.
Referring to Puducherry's exports of US$561 million during 2025–26, she highlighted the Union Territory's potential to further expand its export base and strengthen its presence in international markets. She encouraged Puducherry exporters, particularly MSMEs, to explore emerging opportunities across various sectors and make effective use of preferential market access under FTAs.
She also highlighted the importance of leveraging the Government of India's Export Promotion Mission to enhance the competitiveness of Puducherry's exporters, diversify export markets and contribute to the Union Territory's overall export growth.
Deputy DGFT Shri. Palani Phani kiran, ITS explained the benefits accruing to MSME exporters from the Export Promotion Mission, especially how the LIFT scheme for reimbursing logistics cost has been extended to Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam districts. He emphasized on how the potential of EPM can be maximised by synergizing it with the Districts as Export Hubs initiative.

Himalayan marmot droppings could reveal clues about climate change
articles.full_content:
A new study has probed pollen grains, fungal spores and elemental signatures in the faeces of the Himalayan marmot ( Marmota himalayana ) to trace valuable information on the environmental conditions of the higher Himalaya and how climate change has affected them.
The Himalaya is highly sensitive to changes in temperature, precipitation and snow cover, which can have a significant impact on alpine vegetation and wildlife habitats. Most conventional palaeoenvironmental studies are based on lake sediments, peat and soil. Scientists from Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), an Autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), explored the potential of faeces of Himalayan marmot as an alternative biological archive for environmental changes with climate footprints. This could be especially valuable in remote, arid mountain environments where conventional sedimentary archives are rare.
The Himalayan marmot, a type of herbivorous mammal living at high altitudes in the cold and dry alpine environment of the Himalayan region, relies on local vegetation for food and shelter.
Pollen preserved in the faeces of marmots has left the footprints of the composition of plants consumed by the animal and provides information about the surrounding alpine-steppe vegetation.
The important plant groups in the diet of the marmot were Artemisia , Asteroideae, Caryophyllaceae, Poaceae, Cyperaceae and Chenopodiaceae .
Fig 1. Field photographs- a and b. Alpine steppe vegetation at Pensila Pass in the Himalayan marmot habitat area. c. A Himalayan marmot in their natural habitat in Pensila Pass area. d. Alpine steppe vegetation in Rimkhim area. e. A Himalayan marmot in natural habitat in Rimkhim area. f. Midden faeces of Marmota himalayana , g. Shape and size of the marmot’s faeces pellet.
Photograph credits by Hukam Singh, Manish Mehta, and Vinit Kumar.
Researchers Sadhan K Basumatary, Hukam Singh, Manish Mehta, Swati Tripathi, Mahesh G. Thakkar, H. Gregory McDonald, Eline N. van Asperen & Vinit Kumar identified pollen grains and fungal spores preserved in faeces through palynological analysis, statistical methods for comparing samples from two Himalayan regions and Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy coupled with Energy-Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (FESEM–EDS) to identify elemental composition.
They first evaluated ratios of three types of pollens: Artemisia / Chenopodiaceae , Artemisia / Cyperaceae and Artemisia / Ephedra , for vegetation and climate interpretation based on faecal samples of marmots.
The results indicated that the mixed plant-based diet was dominated by groups like Artemisia , Asteroideae, Caryophyllaceae and Chenopodiaceae , pointing toward alpine vegetation and related environmental conditions. Based on the generated data, it was found that the Himalayan marmot could be a strong indicator species for understanding vegetation and climate changes in the higher Himalaya.

PIB, JKPCC organise press briefing on implementation of Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026
articles.full_content:
Speakers stress source segregation, scientific waste processing and public participation for effective implementation
The Press Information Bureau (PIB), Jammu, in collaboration with the Jammu and Kashmir Pollution Control Committee (JKPCC), today organised a press briefing on the implementation of the Solid Waste Management (SWM) Rules, 2026, to highlight their key provisions and sensitise the media and public about the responsibilities of various stakeholders. The speakers emphasised that source segregation, scientific processing, recycling and active public participation are essential for effective waste management and achieving the objectives of Swachh Bharat.
Chairman, JKPCC, Shri Vasu Yadav, highlighted the major provisions of the new Rules, which place greater emphasis on segregation of waste at source into four categories—wet, dry, sanitary and special care waste. He said the framework seeks to strengthen scientific waste processing, recycling, resource recovery and remediation of legacy dumpsites while ensuring greater accountability among waste generators.
Shri Yadav said the Rules provide for measures such as user fees, spot fines and environmental compensation to ensure compliance. Stressing the need for coordinated action, he called for greater involvement of government agencies, institutions, commercial establishments and citizens in adopting responsible waste management practices.
In her opening remarks, Director, PIB Jammu, Ms. Neha Jalali, said the press briefing was organised to familiarise media organisations and the public with the provisions of the Rules and promote awareness about responsible waste disposal. She emphasised that effective implementation would require behavioural change and active participation of citizens, institutions and local authorities. Ms Jalali also highlighted the important role of media in disseminating information, encouraging source segregation and taking the message of cleanliness and sustainable waste management to the grassroots to achieve Swachh Bharat.
Commissioner, Jammu Municipal Corporation (JMC), Ms. Ayushi Sudan, highlighted the Corporation's initiatives to strengthen waste management and improve accountability among bulk waste generators. She said bulk waste generators have to mandatorily register through a dedicated online portal, adding that this facilitates monitoring and ensure compliance with prescribed norms. She stressed the need to promote recycling, reuse and scientific processing, adding that waste should be viewed as a resource rather than merely a disposal burden.
Ms. Sudan said violations of prescribed norms by bulk waste generators, including dumping waste in public places, attract a penalty of ₹10,000 per violation, besides user charges of ₹5,000. She also highlighted the use of GPS-enabled vehicles for monitoring waste collection and improving operational efficiency. Encouraging public participation, she urged citizens to use the ‘My Jammu’ mobile application to register

MSDE Engages with UN Special Rapporteur on advancing inclusive skilling and economic participation of persons with disabilities
articles.full_content:
Dialogue focuses on accessible training, meaningful employment and pathways to economic independence
The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) held an interaction with Ms. Heba Hagrass, United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, on strengthening disability inclusion in skill development and expanding pathways to employment and entrepreneurship. The engagement formed part of the Special Rapporteur’s official visit to India.
The interaction provided an opportunity to examine how skill development systems can support the dignity, autonomy and economic participation of persons with disabilities. The dialogue centred on addressing barriers across the journey from access to training and certification to employment, retention and career progression, in keeping with the principles of the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD).
Speaking on the engagement, Shri Niranjan Kumar Sudhansu, Additional Secretary, MSDE said, “An inclusive skill ecosystem must recognise both the diversity of learners and the equal worth of their aspirations. For persons with disabilities, access to training must translate into the freedom to choose a vocation, demonstrate competence and progress in the world of work. Our endeavour is to embed accessibility across the skilling journey and strengthen the connection between learning and livelihoods. The measure of our progress must be the opportunities people are able to exercise and the economic independence they are able to achieve.”
The engagement brought into focus the importance of accessible training infrastructure, digital learning platforms, learning materials and assessment processes. Reasonable accommodation, assistive technologies and the capacity of trainers and assessors were identified as important considerations in enabling learners with different disabilities to participate on an equal basis. The discussions also underscored the importance of embedding accessibility and appropriate support within mainstream training programmes, alongside disability-specific interventions, to enable greater participation and inclusion.
The dialogue also addressed the relationship between skilling and labour market inclusion. Industry engagement, accessible workplaces and support during the transition from training to employment are critical to ensuring that acquired skills lead to sustained livelihoods. The discussions also emphasised upon the enabling measures to enhance the participation of persons with disabilities in skill training and government employment, while encouraging greater inclusion and employment opportunities in the private sector.
Entrepreneurship and self-employment were also discussed as important pathways to economic independence, including the role of access to finance, mentoring, technology and markets in supporting entrepreneurs with disabilities.

The engagement formed part of the Special Rapporteur’s official visit to India.

Department of Commerce Amends Guidelines of Four Interventions under Export Promotion Mission to Enhance Support for Exporters
articles.full_content:
The Department of Commerce has amended the guidelines of four interventions under the Niryat Disha sub-scheme of Export Promotion Mission (EPM) on 17 November 2026 to enhance support for exporters and broaden participation. These interventions are Market Access Support (MAS), Trade Regulations, Accreditation & Compliance Enablement (TRACE), and Logistics Interventions for Freight and Transport (LIFT).
The MAS intervention aims to strengthen India's export market access through structured support for activities such as Buyer-Seller Meets (BSMs), Reverse Buyer-Seller Meets (RBSMs), trade fairs, exhibitions and other related market access initiatives.
The amended guidelines provide for the following changes:
● The maximum eligible export turnover for availing airfare reimbursement for participation in Buyer-Seller Meets, trade fairs and trade delegations has been increased from ₹75 lakh in the preceding year to ₹50 crore.
● Airfare reimbursement has been enhanced to up to 95% for Micro and Small Exporters and up to 80% for other eligible exporters.
● The mandatory membership period with Export Promotion Councils has been reduced from six months to three months.
The TRACE intervention provides support to MSMEs in meeting internationally recognised quality, safety and technical requirements applicable in overseas markets. The support covers compliance- and quality-related certifications, as well as other mandatory and voluntary conformity-assessment requirements.
Under the amended guidelines, the list of certificates eligible for reimbursement has been expanded from 462 to 600, enabling wider coverage and greater support for MSMEs in meeting international quality, safety and technical requirements.
The LIFT intervention seeks to address geographical disadvantages and logistics gaps faced by MSMEs in low export-intensity areas by providing support to reduce freight and transportation costs arising from locational challenges.
The amended guidelines provide for the following changes:
● The coverage of low export-intensity districts has been expanded from 13 States/UTs to 34 States/UTs.
● The categories of eligible ports have been expanded to include Land Customs Stations (LCSs) and Integrated Check Posts (ICPs).
● Waterways have been added to the existing modes of transport, namely road, rail and air.
● Air freight support for export shipments has been extended to Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, in addition to the existing coverage of the North Eastern Region.
● The minimum distance eligibility criterion between the origin and destination ports has been reduced from 200 km to 100 km.
● Support has been extended to all exportable merchandise items, except those specified in the negative list of export products/categories of exports.

India calls for Equity, Climate Justice and Fulfilment of Climate Finance Obligations at UNFCCC COP31, at Antalya (Türkiye)
articles.full_content:
Global South cannot be made to Bear Burden of Historical Emissions in name of ‘Higher Ambition’: Shri Bhupender Yadav India stresses Equitable Access to Remaining Carbon Budget and firmly anchors Climate Action in CBDR-RC
Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, delivering India's National Statement at the UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, called for climate action rooted in equity, climate justice and the principle of Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC). Emphasising the COP31 theme of ‘Dialogue, Consensus and Action’, the Minister said that honest dialogue, equity-based consensus and urgent action must guide global climate efforts.
Highlighting the historical responsibility for climate change, Shri Yadav stated that the planet's warming is the consequence of two centuries of industrialisation and economic growth in some countries, fuelled by unabated greenhouse gas emissions. Expecting the Global South to bear the burden of addressing the consequences of these historical emissions in the name of ‘higher ambition’ is unjustified, he asserted. The Minister underlined that developing countries cannot be asked to choose between climate action and their legitimate right to development, decent living standards, health and education, adding that equitable access to the remaining carbon budget is non-negotiable.
Shri Yadav stressed that COP decisions and their implementation must be firmly grounded in equity and CBDR-RC. He called for the Mitigation Work Programme (MWP) to remain facilitative and non-prescriptive, the Global Stocktake (GST) to continue serving as an instrument for informing Parties, and the Just Transition Mechanism (JTM) to be anchored in equity. The Minister also cautioned against unilateral trade measures that penalise developing countries under the guise of climate action and called upon developed countries to honestly and expeditiously fulfil their climate finance obligations.
Highlighting India's climate commitments under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, Shri Yadav said that India's Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) are aligned with the vision of achieving ‘Viksit Bharat’ by 2047 in a sustainable manner. He also emphasised the need to account for climatic and demographic changes and technological advancements while shaping contemporary cooperation. Stressing that the success of COP31 must be assessed through tangible implementation, the delivery of resources to those who need them and the scaling up of proven solutions, Shri Yadav called for dialogue to build trust, consensus to uphold equity and action to deliver climate justice.

India's Wind Energy Transition
articles.full_content:
Charting Path towards 156 GW and Beyond
Wind Energy: Expanding Capacity, Strengthening Energy Security
Wind energy is emerging as a key pillar of India’s transition towards a cleaner and more sustainable energy future. By harnessing the natural movement of air to generate electricity, wind power offers a renewable alternative to fossil fuels . It can help meet growing electricity demand while reducing dependence on conventional energy sources. As India expands its renewable energy capacity, wind energy is becoming increasingly important for building a diverse, resilient and low-carbon emission system.
As of 30 September 2026, India’s total installed renewable energy capacity stood at 299.25 GW . Wind power accounted for 59.20 GW , representing approximately 19.8% of the total installed renewable energy capacity. Between March 2014 and September 2026, installed wind capacity grew from 21 GW to 59.20 GW, nearly a 2.8-fold increase , reflecting wind energy’s growing role in India’s renewable electricity mix.
With continued capacity addition, technological advancement and supportive government initiatives, wind energy is expected to remain a key pillar of India’s efforts to diversify its energy mix, strengthen energy security and achieve its renewable energy targets.
India’s Wind Energy Landscape
India’s wind energy sector is expanding steadily with rising installed capacity and strong wind resource potential across key states. It is increasingly supported by domestic manufacturing and its role in meeting renewable energy targets.
Wind Resource Potential
• India's estimated gross wind power potential is 695.5 GW at 120 metres and 1,163.9 GW at 150 metres above ground level.
• Majority of the assessed wind potential at 150 Meter is concentrated in eight high-resource states: Rajasthan: 284.2 GW; Gujarat: 180.8 GW; Maharashtra : 173.9 GW; Karnataka: 169.3 GW; Andhra Pradesh : 123.3 GW; Tamil Nadu: 95.1 GW; Madhya Pradesh: 55.4 GW; Telangana: 54.7 GW.
• More than 900 wind-monitoring stations have been installed nationwide by NIWE to map wind resources and identify high-potential sites for wind energy development.
• Wind potential maps have been developed at 50 m, 80 m, 100 m, 120 m, and 150 m hub heights .
• India's vast wind resource base provides a strong foundation for achieving 100 GW wind capacity by 2030 and 156 GW by 2036.
Wind Capacity and Manufacturing Growth
• India ranks 4th globally in installed wind power capacity.
• Wind energy capacity has more than doubled over the past 12 years.
• An additional 28 GW is under implementation.
• India recorded its highest-ever annual wind capacity addition of 6.05 GW in 2025-26 , surpassing the previous record of 5.4 GW in 2016-17 .
• Nearly 45% of wind generation occurs during peak demand hours , complementing solar power and strengthening grid reliability.
• Wind Turbine Manufacturing Capacity has increased from 10 GW in 2014 to about 24 GW, as on March 2026.
• The sector has achieved 70-80% indigenisat

By harnessing the natural movement of air to generate electricity, wind power offers a renewable alternative to fossil fuels . India calls for an Open, Transparent and Equitable Second Global Stocktake under Paris Agreement; Presses for Accountability on Climate Finance and Technology Transfer, at COP31 in Antalya (Türkiye)
articles.full_content:
GST-2 must take Comprehensive View of Climate Action, recognise Implementation Gaps and deliver Solution-oriented Outcomes: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Antalya (Türkiye), 18th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, has called for the Second Global Stocktake (GST-2) under the Paris Agreement to be an open, transparent and inclusive process, grounded in the best available science and equity, and delivering balanced outcomes across all aspects of climate action.
Addressing the High-Level Event on the Second Global Stocktake at UNFCCC COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye, the Minister said that the GST must take a comprehensive 360-degree view of the Paris Agreement and its implementation, taking stock of both achievements and existing gaps. He emphasised that the process must be guided by the principles of equity, Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities (CBDR-RC), with developed countries taking the lead in the light of national circumstances.
Shri Yadav highlighted that the Second GST provides an opportunity to assess progress across key areas, including updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), Biennial Transparency Reports, international cooperation under Article 6, the Global Goal on Adaptation and the Just Transition Mechanism. He also stressed the importance of recognising scientific assessments and reports, particularly those emerging from developing countries, alongside IPCC reports.
The Minister emphasised that the GST-2 must examine why, despite progress in climate action, the world remains at risk of crossing the 1.5°C warming threshold in the coming years. He called for solution-oriented outcomes that guide Parties in updating their NDCs and address gaps in the means of implementation, particularly climate finance and technology transfer. He underlined that actual delivery in these areas has fallen far below the obligations and responsibilities of developed countries.
Concluding his address, Shri Yadav expressed India's expectation that the Second Global Stocktake would be conducted successfully and provide a balanced assessment of global climate action and implementation.

Two-day Regional Conclave brings together representatives from 11 Himalayan states to address integrated water and sanitation management, climate resilience and ecosystem-based urban development Ten initiatives, publications and learning resources launched; 18 innovative urban solutions recognised under अrban Learnathon 2.0
The Parvat Manthan Conclave 2026, convened by the National Institute of Urban Affairs (NIUA), concluded today in Dehradun, Uttarakhand, with recommendations to strengthen urban resilience, ecological planning and sustainable service delivery across the Indian Himalayan Region. The two-day Conclave, held from 17 to 18 November 2026, brought together policymakers, representatives from Himalayan states, urban local bodies, technical experts, academia, civil society organisations and development partners to deliberate on the distinct challenges of mountain urbanisation and identify practical approaches for resilient and sustainable urban development.
The Conclave was inaugurated on 17 November 2026 by Shri Tokhan Sahu, Hon’ble Minister of State for Housing and Urban Affairs, Government of India, under the theme ‘From Water Security to Ecosystem-Based Urban Development: Mainstreaming Resilient Water and Sanitation for Himalayan Cities’ .
Delivering the inaugural address, Shri Tokhan Sahu emphasised the importance of regional cooperation, institutional capacity building and knowledge-sharing in addressing the challenges faced by Himalayan cities. Stating that “by pooling knowledge, strengthening local capacities and learning from each other, we can advance solutions for water security, inclusive urban services and dignified sanitation, recognising that challenges do not stop at geographical boundaries”, he called for stronger collaboration among governments, institutions and regional stakeholders. Highlighting the importance of replicating successful urban innovations, he observed that “a solution confined to one city benefits only that city, but a solution shared and replicated has the potential to transform a hundred cities”.
Shri Nitesh Jha, Secretary, Urban Development, Government of Uttarakhand noted that as the source of the Ganga, the Yamuna and other major rivers, Uttarakhand bears a responsibility to every town and village downstream. For this reason, he said, the state treats the management of used water and faecal sludge as a commitment rather than a municipal chore. Tracing the state-led partnership with NIUA since 2019, he highlighted the Septage Management Protocol of 2017 and the co-treatment of septage at existing sewage treatment plants in Ganga towns. He also cited Rudrapur’s faecal sludge treatment plant, the first standalone facility in the state, which was built with support from NIUA. He called on partners, Union ministries and hill states to help design norms and financing that recognise the realities of mountain terrain. articles.full_content:
Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India facilitated the participation of Seven Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) from state of Assam and Meghalaya in the 45 th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026, being held from 14th to 27th November 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi.
The participating MSEs are sponsored by the Ministry MSME under the Procurement and Marketing Support (PMS) Scheme. MSME DFO Guwahati and its Branch offices in Assam and Meghalaya extended all necessary support and facilitation to enable the MSEs participation in this trade fair.
Under this year’s theme “Vikas aur Virasat,” the trade fair provides opportunity to participating MSMEs from various states to showcase their regional products, local industries, traditional crafts, culture, tourism potential and development initiatives. The participation is expected to enhance business visibility, facilitate networking with potential buyers and create avenues for market expansion. Assam along with Delhi, Jharkhand and West Bengal are among the four Focus States.
Manas Small industry from Bajali, Assam and Natural Wood Crafts from Silchar, Assam are engaged in crafting a diverse range of furniture and decorative products made from wood, cane and bamboo.
Megha Creation from East Khasi Hills, Meghalaya manufactures decorative flowers made from locally sourced soft wood and palm leaves. They are environmentally sustainable and showcase traditional knowledge and skills.
Other enterprises from Assam include Tarali Shilp Kala and Mohura by Bhargabi from Kamrup, Sahara Reshom Handloom & Handicraft from Goalpara and Moupiya Silk Handloom, Kamrup Metro. They are representing Assam’s unique handloom and handicraft products which includes products made from Muga silk, Eri silk, Assamese Gamosa etc.
Ministry of MSME is providing an opportunity for a local MSME to showcase its potential at a national-level platform. This initiative reflects the Ministry’s continued efforts towards promoting MSMEs from the North East Region and facilitating their access to wider markets and business opportunities.
The selected entrepreneurs from North East Region are showcasing to the world its vibrant culture, heritage and vast repository of local knowledge crafted into beautiful products in a sustainable manner.

articles.title: One-day PM Vishwakarma Marketing and Branding awareness programme held in Sivasagar by Ministry of MSME
articles.full_content:
The Branch MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Diphu, under MSME-DFO Guwahati, Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of MSME, Government of India, organised a One-Day PM Vishwakarma Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing in collaboration with the District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC), Sivasagar, Assam, on 16 November 2026. The programme was conducted with the objective of enhancing the capabilities of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries through awareness of Artificial Intelligence (AI), branding and marketing, e-commerce onboarding, export promotion, institutional credit, entrepreneurship and various MSME support schemes.
Shri Mridul Yadav, IAS, District Commissioner, Sivasagar, inaugurated the programme and addressed the participants. He highlighted the benefits of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and emphasised the importance of skill upgradation, technology adoption, utilisation of Artificial Intelligence, branding and marketing for enhancing the competitiveness and market reach of traditional artisans. He expressed confidence that these initiatives would help artisans access wider markets across the State and beyond.
More than 150 PM Vishwakarma artisans and stakeholders actively participated in the programme. During the programme, enrolment under various Social Security Schemes and Udyam Registration were carried out, while QR Code generation was facilitated by India Post Payments Bank (IPPB). The initiative contributed towards enhancing awareness of Artificial Intelligence, branding, marketing, digital commerce, export opportunities, financial inclusion and government support mechanisms, thereby strengthening sustainable livelihood opportunities for traditional artisans under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme.
articles.summary: The Branch MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Diphu, under MSME-DFO Guwahati, Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of MSME, Government of India, organised a One-Day PM Vishwakarma Awareness Programme on Branding and Marketing in collaboration with the District Industries & Commerce Centre (DICC), Sivasagar, Assam, on 16 November 2026. The programme was conducted with the objective of enhancing the capabilities of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries through awareness of Artificial Intelligence (AI), branding and marketing, e-commerce onboarding, export promotion, institutional credit, entrepreneurship and various MSME support schemes. Shri Mridul Yadav, IAS, District Commissioner, Sivasagar, inaugurated the programme and addressed the participants.
